mainTopic: רבי מאיר's rule on misused הקדש, and how unnamed משניות decide the הלכה on מעשר שני and הקדש
overview: The amud opens by settling an earlier contradiction: two תנאים report רבי יהודה's view differently. עולא, quoting בר פדא, then gives רבי מאיר's rule: הקדש misused on purpose loses its holiness, but misused by accident it does not, except with regard to a קרבן. The גמרא asks why a קרבן would be owed if nothing changed, so רבין gives a better version: accidental misuse removes holiness only when the item was eaten. Next, רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני and רבי יהודה on הקדש, because an unnamed משנה matches each view. The גמרא finds both sources: בית הלל's view on a כרם רבעי shows they hold like רבי מאיר, and the storekeeper case in מעילה matches רבי יהודה. It then tests the ruling with unnamed משניות that seem to follow רבי יהודה on מעשר. Two are deflected, one with the case of טבל and one with the case of a סמדר, but the third, about a buyer who pulled מעשר שני, really does follow רבי יהודה. In the end רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר because a משנה in מסכת עדויות, 'the chosen tractate,' agrees with him.

steps.title: Two תנאים disagree about רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles an earlier contradiction about רבי יהודה's opinion. Two different תנאים reported his view differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי יהודה held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a contradiction it raised just before this point. It says the two sources simply come from two different תנאים who report רבי יהודה's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources seemed to give opposite views in the name of רבי יהודה. Instead of forcing them to agree, the גמרא says each source comes from a different תנא. Each תנא had his own report of what רבי יהודה held, so there is no real contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים, meaning two different teachers of the משנה period
They are
According to, or about the opinion of

phrases.english: They are two tanna'im
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא and the משנה the גמרא compared just before this, which seemed to clash.

phrases.english: and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי נִינְהוּ וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction raised just before this section, on the previous part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different תנאים report the view differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources report one single view of רבי יהודה, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each source comes from a different תנא with his own report of רבי יהודה's view.

steps.title: עולא's version of רבי מאיר's rule on misused הקדש
steps.stepSummary: עולא, quoting בר פדא, says that according to רבי מאיר, הקדש misused on purpose loses its holiness, but misused by accident it does not. The well-known rule that accidental misuse removes holiness applies only to the duty to bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of בר פדא: רבי מאיר used to say that הקדש misused on purpose loses its holiness, and misused by accident does not. When they said that accidental misuse removes holiness, they meant only for the purpose of bringing a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. עולא explains how רבי מאיר understood what happens when someone uses הקדש on purpose or by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains רבי מאיר's ruling in the משנה, where קידושין with הקדש works when done on purpose but not by accident. On purpose, the item becomes ordinary, so the woman receives something of real value. By accident, the item stays holy, and the familiar rule that it 'becomes ordinary' is limited to the person owing a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Property set aside as holy, belonging to the Temple
On purpose, knowingly
By accident, without knowing
Loses its holiness and becomes ordinary
An offering, here the one owed for misusing הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Here, misuse on purpose is what removes the holiness, and accidental misuse does not, which is the opposite of what many people expect.

phrases.english: Ulla said in the name of bar Padda:
Rabbi Meir would say:
Consecrated property misused intentionally becomes desacralized;
misused unwittingly, it is not desacralized.
And they only said that unwitting misuse desacralizes it
with regard to an offering alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּבַר פְּדָא, אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic that explains רבי מאיר's reasoning about הקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, misuse on purpose removes holiness and accidental misuse does not. The rule that accidental misuse removes holiness concerns only the duty to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: Why owe an offering if nothing changed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא's version. If accidental misuse does not remove the holiness at all, why should the person owe a קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the item does not lose its holiness, what is he liable a קרבן for?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the teaching from the previous step. It points out that the two parts of the teaching do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן for misusing הקדש is owed because the person actually took the item out of its holiness. If the item stays fully holy, his action changed nothing. So there is no reason to owe a קרבן, and עולא's version cannot be right as stated.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, seeing that
For what? On what basis?
He is liable, he owes

phrases.english: But since it is not desacralized,
for what is he liable to bring an offering?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאֵין מִתְחַלֵּל, קׇרְבָּן בְּמַאי מִחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of עולא's version in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that accidental misuse removes holiness only for the purpose of a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קרבן is owed only when the misuse actually took the item out of its holiness. If the holiness stays, there is nothing to atone for.

steps.title: רבין's better version: only when eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a different report of בר פדא's teaching. The rule that accidental misuse removes holiness applies only when the person ate the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came, he explained in the name of בר פדא: רבי מאיר used to say that הקדש misused on purpose loses its holiness, and misused by accident does not. When they said that accidental misuse removes holiness, they meant only when the item was eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: Because עולא's version fell apart, the גמרא brings רבין's report of the same teaching. Only the last words change: 'eating' replaces 'קרבן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone eats הקדש, the item is used up completely, so it truly has left its holiness and he owes a קרבן. When he only uses it, for example by giving it as קידושין, the item stays holy. This avoids the problem in step 3, because the קרבן is owed only where real misuse happened.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings with him
He explained
Eating
Only

steps.whatToRemember: The accepted version is רבין's. According to רבי מאיר, accidental misuse removes holiness only when the item was eaten. Otherwise it stays הקדש, so accidental קידושין with הקדש does not work.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came
he explained in the name of bar Padda:
Rabbi Meir would say:
Consecrated property misused intentionally becomes desacralized;
misused unwittingly, it is not desacralized.
And they only said that unwitting misuse desacralizes it
with regard to eating alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין פָּרֵישׁ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּבַר פְּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces עולא's version, which was rejected in step 3, with רבין's report.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different report of the same teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accidental misuse removes holiness only for the purpose of a קרבן, even though the item stays holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Accidental misuse removes holiness only when the item was eaten, which also explains why a קרבן is owed.

steps.title: רב נחמן's ruling: רבי מאיר on מעשר, רבי יהודה on הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב אדא בר אהבה, rules that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני and רבי יהודה on הקדש. In each case, an unnamed משנה follows that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר about מעשר, since an unnamed משנה follows his view. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה about הקדש, since an unnamed משנה follows his view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on the two disputes in the משנה. It splits the ruling, following a different תנא for each topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of thumb is that when a משנה is taught without a name (סתם משנה), the הלכה follows it. For מעשר שני, an unnamed משנה matches רבי מאיר's view that it counts as holy property. For הקדש, an unnamed משנה matches רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows
Here, מעשר שני: the second tithe, eaten in ירושלים
Since, because
The תנא taught us an unnamed משנה, with no opinion attached
Like him, following his view

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: on מעשר שני we follow רבי מאיר, and on הקדש we follow רבי יהודה. In each case the reason is a סתם משנה that matches that view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key rule for deciding הלכה: an unnamed משנה can decide between תנאים, even if this means following different תנאים on related topics.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Meir with regard to tithe,
since the tanna taught us an unattributed mishna like him,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda with regard to consecrated property,
since the tanna taught us an unattributed mishna like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the views to deciding the practical הלכה on the משנה's two disputes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני and רבי יהודה on הקדש, each because a סתם משנה matches that view.

steps.title: Which unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר's view on מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said an unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר. Which משנה is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רב נחמן's claim that an unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's ruling in step 5 rested on there being an unnamed משנה that agrees with רבי מאיר. The גמרא now wants to see that משנה, because the ruling is only as strong as its source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? Which one is meant?
Second tithe, eaten by the owner in ירושלים

phrases.english: The משנה that is like Rabbi Meir regarding tithe,
which one is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר, מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the ruling in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני

steps.title: The משנה about a fourth-year vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in which בית שמאי and בית הלל argue whether a כרם רבעי has the laws of חומש and ביעור, and whether the poor get פרט and עוללות from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: about a fourth-year vineyard, בית שמאי say there is no added fifth and no removal. בית הלל say these laws do apply. בית שמאי also say the poor get the fallen grapes and the small clusters. בית הלל say all of it goes to the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a משנה about a vineyard in its fourth year. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about two things in that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First argument: בית שמאי say a כרם רבעי has no חומש and no ביעור, while בית הלל say it has both, just like מעשר שני. Second argument: בית שמאי say the poor get פרט and עוללות from it, while בית הלל say all of it goes to the winepress, so the poor get nothing. The next steps explain why this משנה follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year, whose fruit is holy and eaten in ירושלים
The extra fifth added when the owner redeems holy produce
The duty to remove leftover holy produce from the house at set times
Single grapes that fall during the harvest, left for the poor
Small, poorly formed grape clusters, left for the poor
Winepress

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: A fourth-year vineyard,
Beit Shammai say:
It does not have the added fifth,
and it does not have removal.
And Beit Hillel say: It does have them.
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לוֹ פֶּרֶט וְיֵשׁ לוֹ עוֹלֵלוֹת.
phrases.english: It has fallen grapes and it has small clusters for the poor.
And Beit Hillel say: All of it goes to the winepress.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by quoting the relevant משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה in פאה about כרם רבעי, where בית הלל's position will turn out to follow רבי מאיר

steps.title: בית הלל learn כרם רבעי from מעשר through 'holy'
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל compare כרם רבעי to מעשר שני because the תורה calls both 'קדש'. So כרם רבעי has חומש and ביעור. בית שמאי do not make this comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is בית הלל's reason? They learn 'holy' and 'holy' from מעשר. Just as מעשר has an added fifth and removal, a fourth-year vineyard also has an added fifth and removal. בית שמאי do not learn 'holy' and 'holy' from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בית הלל say a כרם רבעי has חומש and ביעור. The תורה uses the word 'holy' for both the vineyard and מעשר, so they share the same laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word in two places links the two topics. Because of this link, בית הלל treat כרם רבעי just like מעשר שני. That matters for the next step, since how בית הלל view מעשר will decide how they view the vineyard.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn it, derive it
Holy, the shared word that links the two topics
Learning one law from another through a shared word in the תורה

phrases.english: What is the reason of Beit Hillel?
They learn 'holy' and 'holy' from tithe,

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר יֵשׁ לוֹ חוֹמֶשׁ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בִּיעוּר –
phrases.english: just as tithe has the added fifth and has removal,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי יֵשׁ לוֹ חוֹמֶשׁ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בִּיעוּר.
phrases.english: so too a fourth-year vineyard has the added fifth and has removal.
And Beit Shammai do not learn
'holy' and 'holy' from tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the first argument in the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית הלל compare כרם רבעי to מעשר through the shared word 'קדש', and בית שמאי do not

steps.title: בית הלל must follow רבי מאיר's view of מעשר
steps.stepSummary: Since בית הלל treat כרם רבעי like מעשר and say all of it goes to the winepress, they must hold that מעשר is holy property. That is רבי מאיר's view, not רבי יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say the vineyard is like מעשר. Whose view of מעשר do they hold? If they held like רבי יהודה, why would all of it go to the winepress? He said מעשר is ordinary private money! So they must hold like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that בית הלל follow רבי מאיר on מעשר שני. This completes the answer to the question of which unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that מעשר שני is ordinary private property. If so, a vineyard compared to it would also be ordinary property, and the poor should get פרט and עוללות. But בית הלל say all of it goes to the winepress, so they must view מעשר, and the vineyard, as holy property, which is רבי מאיר's view. Since we usually follow בית הלל, this משנה backs רב נחמן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion do they hold?
Ordinary private property, not holy
Rather, is it not so that...? (introduces the only option left)

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל compare כרם רבעי to מעשר and give the poor nothing from it. That only makes sense if מעשר is holy property, which is רבי מאיר's view. So the הלכה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't get mixed up: רבי יהודה is the one who says מעשר is ordinary money (ממון הדיוט). רבי מאיר says it is holy property, and that is why no gifts go to the poor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the source of רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני. The proof works because the הלכה usually follows בית הלל.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel, who say it is like tithe,
whose view do they hold?
If they hold like Rabbi Yehuda,
why does all of it go to the winepress?
But he said tithe is ordinary private property!
Rather, isn't it that they hold like Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים כְּמַעֲשֵׂר, כְּמַאן סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the comparison from step 8 together with בית הלל's ruling about the winepress to show they follow רבי מאיר
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's claim that an unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל's ruling in the משנה that all of a כרם רבעי goes to the winepress, which only fits if מעשר is holy property

steps.title: Which unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה on הקדש?
steps.stepSummary: Having found the משנה for רבי מאיר on מעשר שני, the גמרא now asks for the משנה that follows רבי יהודה on הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה regarding הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of רב נחמן's ruling and asks where we find an unnamed משנה that agrees with רבי יהודה about הקדש. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן claimed that each of his two rulings matches an unnamed משנה. The first one, רבי מאיר on מעשר שני, was shown in steps 7-9. Now the גמרא looks for proof of the second one.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that has been made holy and given to the בית המקדש
What is it? Which one is it?

phrases.english: And the one following Rabbi Yehuda regarding consecrated property, which is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proof for רבי מאיר on מעשר to the parallel search for רבי יהודה on הקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The unnamed משנה that follows רבי יהודה on הקדש.

steps.title: The storekeeper who unknowingly spends הקדש money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in מעילה: a man sent הקדש money with a competent agent and then remembered. The storekeeper who later spends it is guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If he sent it with a competent person and remembered before the agent reached the storekeeper, the storekeeper commits מעילה when he spends it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a משנה about a man who accidentally sent holy money with an agent. The storekeeper who receives the money and spends it without knowing is the one who commits מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The storekeeper has no idea that the money is holy, so he acts unknowingly. The משנה still makes him liable for מעילה. This fits רבי יהודה's view that מעילה, and with it the money becoming regular property, happens through unknowing use.

keyTerms.meaning: A competent adult, as opposed to a deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person, or a minor
Storekeeper
Committed מְעִילָה, the misuse of holy property

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he sent it in the hand of a competent person
phrases.notes: The case is a man who mistakenly gave his agent holy money to buy something with.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִזְכַּר עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ אֵצֶל חֶנְווֹנִי –
phrases.english: and he remembered before the agent reached the storekeeper,
the storekeeper commits misuse when he spends it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שִׁילַּח בְּיַד פִּיקֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unnamed משנה in מעילה, where the storekeeper commits מעילה through unknowing use, matches רבי יהודה on הקדש.

steps.title: But a משנה seems to follow רבי יהודה on מעשר too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: there seems to be an unnamed משנה that follows רבי יהודה on מעשר שני. It concerns someone who redeems מעשר שני that he received as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn a משנה that follows רבי יהודה on מעשר? We did learn: One who redeems his own מעשר שני adds a fifth, whether the produce was his own or given to him as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge. It quotes a משנה about adding a fifth when redeeming מעשר שני, including מעשר שני that the person got as a gift. The next step will explain why this משנה looks like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני. If another unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה on מעשר שני, the support for רב נחמן's ruling is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn? (introduces a challenging source)
One who redeems, meaning he moves the holiness onto money
Its fifth, the extra amount added when an owner redeems
Gift

phrases.english: But following Rabbi Yehuda regarding tithe,
did we not learn a mishna?
But we did learn:
One who redeems his own second tithe
adds its fifth to it,
whether it is from his own produce
or it was given to him as a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂר מִי לָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first half of רב נחמן's ruling, after both halves were given sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another unnamed משנה appears to follow רבי יהודה on מעשר שני, so the unnamed משניות do not clearly side with רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why the gift case cannot be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that מעשר is holy property, so a person could not give it as a gift. The משנה must therefore follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי מאיר, can a person give it as a gift? But he said that מעשר is property of the Most High! So isn't it רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its challenge. A gift of מעשר שני only makes sense if מעשר belongs to the person, and that is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, מעשר שני belongs to Heaven, so the owner has no right to give it away. Since the משנה talks about receiving it as a gift, it seems to follow רבי יהודה, who treats מעשר as the person's own property.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
If you say
Property belonging to the Most High, meaning holy property
Rather, is it not...?

phrases.english: Whose view is this? If you say it is Rabbi Meir,
can he give it to him as a gift?
But he said: tithe is property of the Most High!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 12 by showing the משנה cannot fit רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That the gift משנה follows רבי יהודה on מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's principle that מעשר is מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ, which rules out giving it as a gift.

steps.title: The gift was given while the produce was still טבל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can still be רבי מאיר. The person gave untithed produce, and gifts not yet separated do not count as separated, so the produce was not yet holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is רבי מאיר. Here the case is where he gave it to him while it was still טבל, and he holds that gifts not yet separated are treated as not separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge. The משנה is talking about giving produce before the מעשר שני was ever separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before separation, the produce is not seen as a mixture that already contains holy מעשר. It is just regular untithed produce, which the owner may give away. Afterward, the receiver separates and redeems his own מעשר שני, even under רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeps the original position)
What case are we dealing with here?
Produce from which the required gifts have not yet been separated
Gifts, like תרומה and מעשר, that have not yet been separated

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from the gift משנה is answered: the gift was given while the produce was still טבל. Unseparated gifts do not count as already present, so even רבי מאיר agrees the owner may give the produce away.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the owner gave away holy מעשר שני. He gave away untithed produce, and the מעשר שני only came into being when the receiver separated it.

phrases.english: No, really it is Rabbi Meir,
and with what are we dealing here?
Where he gave it to him in its untithed state,
and he holds:
gifts that have not been separated
are considered as if they have not been separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 13 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the gift משנה must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the gift was separated מעשר שני. In fact it was untithed produce, which is not yet holy.

steps.title: A new challenge from redeeming נטע רבעי received as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a parallel משנה: one who redeems his נטע רבעי adds a fifth, whether it was his own or given to him as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who redeems his own נטע רבעי adds a fifth, whether it was his own or given to him as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second challenge, this time from a משנה about fourth-year fruit. The next step will explain why this also looks like רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case looks just like the מעשר case, but it uses fourth-year fruit. The טבל answer may not help here, because fourth-year fruit is holy from the start and nothing needs to be separated from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a new source)
Fruit of a tree or vine in its fourth year, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who redeems his own fourth-year planting
adds its fifth to it,
whether it is from his own,
or it was given to him as a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַפּוֹדֶה נֶטַע רְבָעִי שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מעשר challenge was answered, brings a parallel source where that answer may not work.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר on מעשר שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A gift of נטע רבעי, which is compared to מעשר, appears to follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why the נטע רבעי gift case seems to be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, נטע רבעי is learned from מעשר through the word 'קדש', so it would be holy property that cannot be given as a gift. The משנה therefore seems to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי מאיר, can a person give it to someone? But they learn 'קדש' 'קדש' from מעשר! So isn't it רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the נטע רבעי משנה seems to fit רבי יהודה and not רבי מאיר. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קדש' links נטע רבעי to מעשר, as we saw with בית הלל in step 8. For רבי מאיר, that link makes נטע רבעי holy property, so it could not be given away. Since this fruit is holy from the start, the טבל answer from step 14 does not obviously work.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn (derive one law from another)
The shared word 'holy' used for both נטע רבעי and מעשר, linking their laws

phrases.english: Whose view is this? If you say Rabbi Meir,
can he give it to him?
But they derive 'holy' 'holy' from tithe!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 15 by showing it cannot fit רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That the נטע רבעי gift משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'קדש' 'קדש' comparison to מעשר, together with רבי מאיר's view that מעשר is holy property.

steps.title: The gift was given while the fruit was only a bud
steps.stepSummary: The נטע רבעי משנה can still follow רבי מאיר. The gift was given while the fruit was still a סמדר (bud), before it became holy fruit. This works only if we do not hold like רבי יוסי, who treats a bud as fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה follows רבי מאיר. It is talking about a case where the owner gave the fruit away while it was still just a bud. This does not fit רבי יוסי, who says a bud is already forbidden because it already counts as fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 16. It shows how the נטע רבעי משנה can still fit רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that holy נטע רבעי cannot be given as a gift. The answer is that the gift happened at the bud stage, when it was not yet 'fruit' and not yet holy. That only works for those who disagree with רבי יוסי, since he says a bud already counts as fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in fact (it is still the same view)
The tiny early fruit just after the blossom falls
With what case are we dealing?
The תנא who holds that a bud already counts as fruit

phrases.english: Really, it follows Rabbi Meir,
and with what case are we dealing here?
Where he gave it while it was still a bud.
phrases.notes: A סמדר is the tiny fruit that appears right after the flower drops. It is not yet real fruit.

phrases.english: And this is not like Rabbi Yosei,
who says: a bud is forbidden,
because it is already fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 16 by changing what case the משנה describes.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the נטע רבעי משנה must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the gift was real fruit. It may have been given at the bud stage, before it was holy.

steps.title: Another משנה: the buyer who pulled מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another unattributed משנה. A buyer pulled מעשר שני worth one סלע, and its value rose to two before he paid. He pays one סלע and keeps the profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone pulled מעשר שני worth one סלע from the seller. Before he got to redeem it, its price went up to two סלעים. He pays only one סלע, gains a סלע, and the מעשר שני is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה as a challenge to רב נחמן. It is setting up the next step, which will ask whose opinion this משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the buyer pays the old price. That means the deal was locked in the moment he pulled the produce, before any money changed hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a source is being brought)
Pulled: a way of acquiring movable items
A coin of set value
Gains / makes a profit

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he pulled from him tithe worth a sela,
phrases.notes: Pulling the item toward yourself is a normal way to buy movable things.

phrases.english: and he did not manage to redeem it
until its price stood at two,
he gives a sela,
and he gains a sela,
and the second tithe is his.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the נטע רבעי source was deflected, the גמרא brings a new unattributed source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the הלכה on מעשר שני follows רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another unattributed משנה appears to follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Holy property needs payment, so this must be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is holy, and holy property is acquired only when the money is paid. So the buyer should pay the new, higher price. Since the משנה lets him pay the old price, it must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי מאיר, why does the buyer gain a סלע? The תורה says, 'He gives the money and it becomes his.' So it must be רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the משנה from step 18 cannot fit רבי מאיר, so it must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy property is acquired only through payment, not through pulling. For רבי מאיר, the price rose before the buyer owned the produce, so he should owe two. For רבי יהודה, מעשר שני is ordinary property, so pulling acquired it at the old price.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
If you say
And it is established as his (only after paying)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Rather, is it not...

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
If you say Rabbi Meir,
why does he gain a sela?
"And he gives the money and it becomes his"
the Merciful One said!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the משנה in step 18 must follow רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the unattributed משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'וְנָתַן אֶת הַכֶּסֶף וְקָם לוֹ': holy property is acquired only through payment.

steps.title: One unattributed משנה against two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that this משנה follows רבי יהודה. Still, the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, because two unattributed משניות follow him and only one follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי יהודה. But here there is only one unattributed משנה, and there are two unattributed משניות on the other side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It defends רב נחמן by counting the unattributed משניות on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not deflect the proof this time. It accepts it. The new point is that two unattributed משניות for רבי מאיר outweigh the single one for רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed משנה (stated without a name)
One
Two unattributed משניות

phrases.english: Really, it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
but here there is one unattributed mishna,
and there there are two unattributed mishnayot.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָכָא חַד סְתָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 19 but explains why רב נחמן's ruling still stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the source, then outweighs it by counting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One unattributed משנה for רבי יהודה should decide the הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two unattributed משניות for רבי מאיר outweigh one.

steps.title: Why should counting matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the counting answer. If an unattributed משנה is meant to set the הלכה, then one should be as strong as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if an unattributed משנה is meant to set the הלכה, what difference does it make whether there is one or two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unattributed משנה is a deliberate signal of the הלכה. If so, one signal for רבי יהודה should stand against two for רבי מאיר. That leaves a contradiction instead of a decision.

keyTerms.meaning: Precisely / deliberately (meant to set the halacha)
What difference does it make to me

phrases.english: But if an unattributed mishna is deliberate,
phrases.notes: He means the משנה left out the name on purpose, to show what the halacha is.

phrases.english: what difference is it to me, one unattributed mishna
or two unattributed mishnayot?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סְתָמָא דַּוְקָא, מָה לִי חַד סְתָמָא מָה לִי תְּרֵי סְתָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the counting answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that two unattributed משניות outweigh one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each unattributed משנה deliberately sets the הלכה, so their number should not matter.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר because of the chosen tractate
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new reason. The הלכה follows רבי מאיר because a משנה in בחירתא, meaning מסכת עדויות, agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר, since we learned a משנה like him in 'the chosen tractate.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק replaces the counting answer with a stronger reason. This ends the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not about how many משניות there are. It is about which one carries more weight. מסכת עדויות is treated as the authoritative הלכה, so its משנה that follows רבי מאיר decides the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the final reason
'The chosen one': מסכת עדויות
Since / because
Like him (following his view)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר that מעשר שני is holy property. The reason is not the number of unattributed משניות. It is that מסכת עדויות, 'the chosen tractate,' rules like him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a משנה in עדויות carries special weight when deciding the הלכה.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Meir,
since we learned in the chosen tractate like him.
phrases.notes: 'The chosen tractate' means מסכת עדויות, whose rulings are accepted as halacha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר הוֹאִיל וּתְנַן בִּבְחִירָתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 with a new basis for the ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר, because the משנה in מסכת עדויות rules like him.
